s1.syndrome_frame: Subacute onset of systemic inflammation with skin, muscle, and mucous membrane involvement
salient_findings: Facial swelling, dysphagia, and dysarthria
Pruritic rash on trunk and upper extremities
Anasarca and diffuse coalescent erythematous rash
Heliotrope rash and erythematous lip swelling
Progressive shoulder and hip weakness
key_facts: 65-year-old man with history of hepatitis B, hepatitis C, rheumatoid arthritis, chronic obstructive pulmonary disease, hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and obesity
Presented with several months of facial swelling, dysphagia, and dysarthria
Developed pruritic rash on trunk and upper extremities
No personal or family history of angioedema
Medications included lisinopril, atorvastatin, albuterol, and ibuprofen
Discontinued etanercept six months before presentation
Vital signs were stable on arrival
Physical examination notable for anasarca and diffuse coalescent erythematous rash
Elevated C-reactive protein and erythrocyte sedimentation rate
Elevated anti-Sjögren syndrome–related antigen A autoantibodies
High antinuclear antibody titers
Elevated creatine kinase
Positive myositis panel for anti-SAE antibodies
Skin biopsy results consistent with Wong-type presentation

shortlist.label: Dermatomyositis
shortlist.why_kept: Heliotrope rash, erythematous lip swelling, and elevated creatine kinase levels are consistent with dermatomyositis

shortlist.label: Polymyositis
shortlist.why_kept: Elevated creatine kinase levels and muscle weakness are consistent with polymyositis

shortlist.label: Systemic lupus erythematosus
shortlist.why_kept: High antinuclear antibody titers and elevated anti-Sjögren syndrome–related antigen A autoantibodies suggest a possible diagnosis of systemic lupus erythematosus

shortlist.label: Mixed connective tissue disease
shortlist.why_kept: Overlap of symptoms from different autoimmune diseases, such as dermatomyositis, polymyositis, and systemic lupus erythematosus, suggests a possible diagnosis of mixed connective tissue disease

shortlist.label: Anti-synthetase syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: Elevated anti-Sjögren syndrome–related antigen A autoantibodies and myositis panel results suggest a possible diagnosis of anti-synthetase syndrome

raw.rationale: The patient's presentation with facial swelling, dysphagia, dysarthria, and a pruritic rash, along with elevated creatine kinase and a positive myositis panel for anti-SAE antibodies, is consistent with dermatomyositis. The skin biopsy results and the presence of a heliotrope rash further support this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Polymyositis
rejected.why: The presence of a pruritic rash and skin biopsy results consistent with Wong-type presentation are more characteristic of dermatomyositis than polymyositis.

rejected.label: Systemic lupus erythematosus
rejected.why: While the patient has elevated antinuclear antibody titers, the overall clinical presentation and laboratory findings are more consistent with dermatomyositis than systemic lupus erythematosus.

rejected.label: Mixed connective tissue disease
rejected.why: The patient's symptoms and laboratory findings do not meet the criteria for mixed connective tissue disease, which typically involves a combination of features from multiple autoimmune diseases.

rejected.label: Anti-synthetase syndrome
rejected.why: The patient's presentation and laboratory findings do not suggest anti-synthetase syndrome, which is characterized by the presence of anti-synthetase antibodies and a distinct set of clinical features.
